mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower financing costs for corporate expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in reduced economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy enters a sustainable expansion phase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high consumer spending, rising residential construction activity (HOUST) signals robust demand for goods and services, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenues accelerate.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST rises and GDPC1 > 11500.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) indicates strong housing market activity that correlates with rising consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the economy gains momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 115.0, it signals a robust manufacturing sector that supports corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 115.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy enters a strong expansion phase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both rise, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime, a decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tight labor market conditions that boost corporate profit margins, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as wage pressures support consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
